current_identity_transition.preserved_identifiers: Existing Go imports, synon API/schema IDs, scientific component namespaces, service/install roots and user database/state paths remain compatibility identifiers. They do not define the displayed product name or archive identity.
current_identity_transition.current_brand_surfaces: Current UI translations, runtime prompts/errors, CLI/help/report headings, native directory-picker text, installer messages and the adapted bundled browser connector use the root product display name. Unused legacy design-reference images are not shipped as current product assets.
current_identity_transition.retained_source_facts: Original component names, copyright/license notices, adaptation input hashes, immutable import provenance and historical Git commit messages retain their true source identity; scientific synonym fields are not product marks.
current_identity_transition.browser_connector_compatibility: The adapted connector keeps its component version, existing message/storage keys, permissions and origin matches. Existing Synon tab-group titles remain readable, while newly emitted display titles use X-Science. The precise legacy bundled relative-package setting is resolved to the current archive; custom and absolute operator package paths are not rewritten.
current_identity_transition.rollback: Revert the focused identity candidate or restore the preceding identified artifact; the shared source-launcher alias does not create a new state owner. GitHub name changes preserve repository ID/history and can be reversed as a separate settings operation.

phases.scope: governance authority and fail-closed inventory gate
phases.rollback: revert the focused governance commit; no runtime or data change

phases.scope: user-visible README, frontend descriptions, UI, CLI and API metadata consume the root-derived product display
phases.predecessor: IDENTITY-0 plus exact Core and UX file leases
phases.rollback: revert projection commits before release; no alias removal

phases.scope: build, package and manifest versions consume or verify the root authority
phases.rollback: restore prior projection commit and artifacts; published tags are never rewritten

phases.scope: optional binary, service, package, install-path and module renames
phases.predecessor: complete consumer graph, compatibility aliases, platform install/upgrade and rollback evidence
phases.rollback: retain old launchers and paths until the new identity is independently verified; persisted identifiers use forward migration or backup restore

phases.scope: create the release tag derived from the root authority
phases.predecessor: User-authorized clean release candidate with all mandatory gates and a signed external receipt bound to exact artifacts
phases.rollback: not applicable: tags and published artifacts are immutable; a bad release is superseded

never_blind_replace: SQLite filenames, table values and migration journal entries
service names, install roots and user state paths
schema, API, asset and third-party dependency versions
